prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the root cause directly in _initialize() by calling context.update_token_expiry() on the loaded tokens, a 4-line change with a new expired_tokens test fixture covering the exact scenario. #2875 treats the symptom instead: it adds a whole new refresh-before-reauth branch inside async_auth_flow's 401 handler, and its own inline comment states the reason is precisely the missing token_expiry_time restoration that #1784 fixes at the source. prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client is exhausted (max attempts reached) or otherwise fails, the pending request is never resolved and the caller hangs forever instead of receiving an error. #2395 fixes '_handle_reconnection' by constructing a JSONRPCError and sending it through 'read_stream_writer' so the caller's pending request resolves with an in-band JSON-RPC error. #3098 instead has the reconnection path raise a 'StreamableHTTPError' and adds a new '_unwrap_exception' helper to dig that error out of anyio ExceptionGroups so it can be re-raised to the caller. These are two different fixes for the same root cause (reconnection failure isn't surfaced to the waiting caller). (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: Resolves the pending request with a proper JSON-RPC error object via the existing read_stream_writer path, matching the same JSONRPCError/ErrorData/INTERNAL_ERROR pattern independently used by PR #3092 for the analogous non-2xx-response case, so the codebase ends up with one consistent error-surfacing convention. #3098's approach instead introduces a new '_unwrap_exception' helper to pull a StreamableHTTPError out of anyio ExceptionGroups, which is a larger, more invasive change to the client's error-propagation contract (raised exception vs. in-band JSON-RPC error) for the same underlying bug, and its diff also includes an unrelated '__future__ import' line change suggesting it wasn't rebased as cleanly.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client is exhausted (max attempts reached) or otherwise fails, the pending request is never resolved and the caller hangs forever instead of receiving an error. #2395 fixes '_handle_reconnection' by constructing a JSONRPCError and sending it through 'read_stream_writer' so the caller's pending request resolves with an in-band JSON-RPC error. #3098 instead has the reconnection path raise a 'StreamableHTTPError' and adds a new '_unwrap_exception' helper to dig that error out of anyio ExceptionGroups so it can be re-raised to the caller. These are two different fixes for the same root cause (reconnection failure isn't surfaced to the waiting caller). (2 PRs)

members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs patch the same branch in validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) that mishandles the case where a previous assistant tool_use is not followed by any tool_result in the next message — currently this incorrectly raises 'ids do not match' because tool_result_ids ends up empty. The two PRs disagree on the fix: #2962 changes the guard to `has_tool_results and has_previous_tool_use and previous_content`, so the id-match check is skipped entirely and no error is raised when there are no tool_results at all — its added test and comment cite SEP-1577, which requires tool_result to be preceded by tool_use but does not require the reverse. #3053 keeps the existing raising behavior but adds an explicit `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)` with a clearer message, i.e. it still raises, just with better wording. These are not just overlapping edits but functionally opposite outcomes for the same input (silently allow vs. raise with a clearer message), so they can't both be applied. (2 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: 3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the WWW-Authenticate header into top-level comma segments first, then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly locates the segment whose scheme token is 'Bearer' before collecting its params — this correctly handles a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=..., Bearer realm=..., error=...'). 3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat parameter list, which would incorrectly merge params from a second scheme into the first challenge's param list if multiple challenges are present in the header.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client is exhausted (max attempts reached) or otherwise fails, the pending request is never resolved and the caller hangs forever instead of receiving an error. #2395 fixes '_handle_reconnection' by constructing a JSONRPCError and sending it through 'read_stream_writer' so the caller's pending request resolves with an in-band JSON-RPC error. #3098 instead has the reconnection path raise a 'StreamableHTTPError' and adds a new '_unwrap_exception' helper to dig that error out of anyio ExceptionGroups so it can be re-raised to the caller. These are two different fixes for the same root cause (reconnection failure isn't surfaced to the waiting caller). (2 PRs)

members.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs patch the same branch in validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) that mishandles the case where a previous assistant tool_use is not followed by any tool_result in the next message — currently this incorrectly raises 'ids do not match' because tool_result_ids ends up empty. The two PRs disagree on the fix: #2962 changes the guard to `has_tool_results and has_previous_tool_use and previous_content`, so the id-match check is skipped entirely and no error is raised when there are no tool_results at all — its added test and comment cite SEP-1577, which requires tool_result to be preceded by tool_use but does not require the reverse. #3053 keeps the existing raising behavior but adds an explicit `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)` with a clearer message, i.e. it still raises, just with better wording. These are not just overlapping edits but functionally opposite outcomes for the same input (silently allow vs. raise with a clearer message), so they can't both be applied. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: 3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the WWW-Authenticate header into top-level comma segments first, then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly locates the segment whose scheme token is 'Bearer' before collecting its params — this correctly handles a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=..., Bearer realm=..., error=...'). 3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat parameter list, which would incorrectly merge params from a second scheme into the first challenge's param list if multiple challenges are present in the header.

members.cluster_pick_reason: 3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the WWW-Authenticate header into top-level comma segments first, then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly locates the segment whose scheme token is 'Bearer' before collecting its params — this correctly handles a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=..., Bearer realm=..., error=...'). 3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat parameter list, which would incorrectly merge params from a second scheme into the first challenge's param list if multiple challenges are present in the header.
